summary: Stateful customer firewall suppresses DNS/ICMP responses causing model artifact pull failures on Private deploy
description:
Issue summary:
Customer private deployment started failing to pull model artifacts and agent heartbeats intermittently. Failures coincide with DNS failures and ICMP packets being dropped by customer-managed firewall appliances.

Impact:
- Model downloads for new replica launches fail ~15-30% of the time, causing delayed rollouts and increased cold-start latency.
- Agent heartbeat gaps observed on private control plane (heartbeat gaps 10-60s).
- Affects production traffic for inference and autoscaling; customer reports client-facing errors "503 - model not loaded" during spikes.

Environment:
- Private deployment in BrightSignals' VPC (eu-west-1), Redwood Private control plane connecting over VPC peering and a set of firewall appliances in front of subnet where inference agents run.
- Agent version: 1.12.4; serving-runtime: 2.3.1; model registry: artifactstore.svc.internal (DNS CNAME into on-prem cache).

Steps to reproduce:
1) Trigger a new autoscale run by sending 500 concurrent short infer requests to a pinned model.
2) Observe agents spin up new replicas and attempt to pull model artifacts from artifactstore.svc.internal.
3) Capture packet traces and agent logs during replica start.

Observed behavior:
- Agent logs show repeated "DNS resolution failed" and "connection reset during TLS handshake" when attempting to reach artifactstore.svc.internal.
- Packet capture shows DNS A responses being sparsely returned (many queries receive no response) and ICMP fragmentation-needed messages suppressed.
- Firewall (customer-managed) appliance logs show stateful connection entries for UDP/53 timing out and TCP half-open states being torn down after ~12s.

Expected behavior:
- DNS responses should be forwarded reliably to agents and model artifacts pulled successfully within startup window.
- ICMP Path MTU messages should not be silently dropped, allowing correct TCP MSS negotiation for TLS handshakes.

Logs/artifacts attached:
- agent-startup.log excerpts (lines with DNS/TLS errors)
- tcpdump capture (udp port 53 & port 443)
- firewall config extract (anonymized) showing firewall session timeouts

Additional notes:
- Customer confirmed recent firewall policy change two days prior that enabled aggressive stateful inspection and dropped "invalid" UDP fragments.
- Similar symptom patterns previously observed in SUP-24107 (heartbeat loss) but root cause here appears tied to DNS/ICMP suppression rather than route propagation.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Firewall stateful inspection is dropping fragmented UDP responses for DNS; cause: firmware change flagged truncated UDP packets as invalid.
Hypothesis 2: ICMP 'fragmentation needed' (Type 3, Code 4) messages are being blocked at perimeter causing PMTU negotiation failures -> TLS handshake MSS mismatch and connection resets.

Findings: Packet traces show DNS queries retransmitted multiple times before response; many DNS responses are larger than 512 bytes and are fragmented. Firewall logs show 'invalid fragment' entries correlated with timestamps.
Test: Customer increased UDP session timeout and allowed ICMP PMTU messages; model pulls improved immediately but not fully resolved until fragmentation handling adjusted on firewall.
Artifact store: no evidence of artifact corruption; failures localized to connection establishment phase (DNS + TLS).
resolution_notes: Workaround applied (customer): Increased UDP session timeout and relaxed fragmentation inspection on firewall appliance. Immediate customer-reported reduction in failures from ~25% to ~3%.

Permanent fix: Customer will upgrade firewall firmware to vendor-supplied patch that fixes fragmentation handling and will explicitly allow ICMP Type 3 Code 4 for the agent subnets. Change scheduled and tracked by customer change control.

Redwood action items: 1) Add guidance to Private Deploy runbook advising customers to allow PMTU ICMP messages and to properly handle fragmented DNS responses. 2) Create alert in Console for repeated DNS resolution retries during replica startup (to auto-warn on similar issues). 3) Cross-reference with SUP-24107 to update runbook.
Follow-up: Monitor for 48 hours post-change; customer to report SLA metric for model pull success. If residual issues, open deeper packet-level session-trace with vendor support.
